---

## Learning goals

- Lift raw $x$ by a fixed transform $\phi$ and run **linear** ERM in $\phi$-space.
- Recognize polynomial / Fourier-style regression as generalized linear models.
- Link choice of $\phi$ to implicit class-conditional assumptions (Bayes view).
- Preview: neural nets **learn** $\phi$ instead of hand-designing it.

---

## Before this clicks

Naive linear model: $h_\theta(x)=\theta^\top x$. Real relationships may be quadratic, sinusoidal, etc. Idea: map $x\mapsto\phi(x)\in\mathbb{R}^p$ with a **user-chosen** transform, then learn a linear model in the new coordinates.

(Playlist title says “GLS”; the lecture content is **generalized linear models / least squares after feature transforms** — classical “generalized least squares” with a noise covariance is a different topic.)

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Fixed feature map

$$
\tilde x = \phi(x),\qquad \phi:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^p.
$$

Coordinates of $\phi$ may mix several input dimensions (design choice). Transform the whole training set, then solve OLS:

$$
\tilde\theta^\star = \arg\min_{\tilde\theta}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(\tilde\theta^\top\phi(x_i)-y_i\bigr)^2,
$$

with the usual normal-equation solution in the $\phi$-features.

Still “linear regression” in $\tilde x$-space; generally **nonlinear** in original $x$.

### 2. Polynomial example

$x\in\mathbb{R}$, $\phi(x)=(1,x,x^2)^\top$. Then

$$
\tilde\theta^\top\phi(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2
$$

— **polynomial regression** = OLS after a polynomial feature map.

Fourier / sine–cosine expansions are the same pattern with trigonometric $\phi$ (think Fourier series as ERM with those bases).

### 3. Design choices

- What $\phi$ to use (polynomial, wavelet, hand-crafted image/speech features, …).  
- Output dimension $p$ (how many features).  
Historically: entire careers spent on **feature engineering**. Deep nets later learn $\phi$ jointly with the classifier.

### 4. Probabilistic / Bayes link (homework flavor from class)

- Equal-covariance Gaussian class-conditionals $\Rightarrow$ Bayes rule linear in $x$.  
- Unequal covariances $\Rightarrow$ quadratic decision boundary $\Leftrightarrow$ quadratic features in an ERM story.  
Choosing $\phi$ reshapes the implicit distributional assumption behind the linear ERM in feature space.

### 5. Toward neural nets

If mixtures / complex densities need rich features, do not freeze $\phi$: let a network represent $\phi_\psi$ and train end-to-end. That is the “ignorance modeling” path previewed since Lecture 1.

---

## Worked mini-example

Data roughly on a parabola. Linear OLS in raw $x$ underfits. With $\phi(x)=(1,x,x^2)$, OLS in 3-D feature space recovers a quadratic curve while still using the linear closed form in $\tilde\theta$.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Linear in features $\Rightarrow$ linear in $x$ | Only if $\phi$ itself is linear. |
| $p$ must equal $d$ | $p$ is free; often $p>d$. |
| Same as classical GLS (colored noise) | Here “generalized” means **feature-lifted** least squares / GLM-style maps. |
